title: add vpc control plane provisioning: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, Route53 automation
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR implements end-to-end Terraform automation to provision the Private Control Plane VPC and its networking primitives for private deployments: multi-AZ subnets (public/private patterns for control plane components), interface VPC endpoints (SSM, ECR, STS, KMS, S3, Secrets Manager), tightly-scoped security groups for control-plane services, VPC peering automation to customer VPCs, and Route53 private hosted zone association/peering DNS records. Motivation: reduce manual steps in the VPC onboarding runbook, enable reproducible private installs, and ensure we can create predictable network topology for Dedicated/Private customers. Includes: new modules/vpc-control-plane (subnets, route tables, nat gateways optional by az), modules/interface-endpoints (service mapping + endpoint policy), modules/sg-control-plane (least-privilege SGs and reusable rules), peering automation with cloudformation-like acceptance workflow, Route53 association module and automated delegation records, terraform remote-state outputs consumed by the private-installer. Also updates redwood-private-installer to read module outputs, updates redwood-helm-charts values for control-plane private networking, and documents upgrade and rollback procedures. Checklist: design docs linked, terraform fmt/validate, unit tests for module logic, e2e private-installer test in perf-canary, docs update in redwood-docs; security review completed. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour preserves existing single-AZ layouts unless multi_az=true; safe-by-default security groups and ephemeral peering acceptance required. Rollback: destroy is safe but we provide an uninstall plan and documented manual rollback steps for DNS/peering. See release_notes for user-facing notes and the linked Linear tickets for rollout schedule.

release_notes: Add Terraform modules and installer integration to automate provisioning of Private Control Plane VPC: multi-AZ subnet creation, interface endpoints for required AWS services, least-privilege security groups, VPC peering automation, and Route53 private hosted zone association. Default behavior unchanged until multi_az=true. Provides outputs consumed by the private-installer and docs for upgrade/rollback.
security_impact: Low: added scoped endpoint policies and tightened SG defaults; security review completed and mitigations documented.
testing: Unit tests for CIDR and subnet allocation logic
Terraform validate/plan in CI on modules
Private-installer e2e deployed control plane into perf-canary VPC and validated DNS resolution and peering acceptance
Manual security validation for endpoint policies and SGs in staging
upgrade_instructions: To upgrade existing private deployments: 1) run terraform apply with existing state (module defaults preserve single-AZ layout), 2) verify outputs for control_plane_vpc_id and route53_association_id, 3) run redwood-private-installer with --tf-outputs pointing to the updated state, 4) perform smoke tests described in redwood-docs/private/vpc-provisioning.md. For rollback, follow the documented manual steps to disassociate Route53 before destroying peering resources to avoid DNS orphaning.
